summary: Root cause identified with medium confidence (0.68, capped by the Critic): payment-service's mTLS client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal expired at 2026-04-02T12:15:00Z, and every subsequent outbound call to bank-partner-api was rejected with TLS alert 45 (expired certificate). Onset is pinned to a single bucket — bank_api_error_rate stepped 0.2%→100% and payment_success_rate collapsed 99.7%→2.5% at 12:15:00Z — and all 311 payment-service ERRORs carry the identical expired-client-cert signature naming our own cert and notAfter stamp. The dashboard stayed green because the error_rate metric only counts HTTP 5xx while failed transfers are marked PENDING_RETRY internally (failures occur on the bank egress, outside the synchronous request path). The origin is localized to payment-service's own client-credential lifecycle: no renewal artifact (no cert-manager/secret entity, zero payment-service deployments, no cert-related config change) exists anywhere in the change feed, and no sibling service shows a matching TLS/bank symptom. Two residual details remain unfalsifiable with available telemetry (never-renewed vs. renewed-but-not-reloaded; a coincident bank-side event), carried as assumptions.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Expired payment-service mTLS client certificate rejected by bank-partner-api (credential_expiry)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: payment-service's client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal reached notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z without a working renewal/reload, so from that instant every outbound call to bank-partner-api is rejected with TLS alert 45 (expired certificate). Transfers fail at the bank egress while the synchronous HTTP error_rate panel stays green because failures are marked PENDING_RETRY internally rather than surfaced as 5xx. Origin is payment-service's own client-credential lifecycle (no renewal artifact exists in the change feed: no cert-rotation deployment, no secret-mount/config change, no cert-manager entity). The precise sub-origin (never renewed vs. renewed-but-not-reloaded) remains the one open detail and is carried as an assumption, not split into a separate hypothesis.

causal_chain.claim: A cert-watcher WARN at 11:50:26Z announces the client cert expires in 25 minutes (notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z) — the expiry clock was already running and no renewal had taken effect

No renewal artifact exists anywhere in the change feed: exactly one deployment in the whole window (dep-5510 settlement-service v1.9.0, 10:30Z) and exactly one config change (cfg-2502 bank.api.timeout_ms, 11:20Z), neither touching payment-service's TLS credential; no cert-manager/rotation entity is queryable at all
At notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z the certificate expires and bank-partner-api begins rejecting the mTLS handshake
bank_api_error_rate steps from ~0.2% to 100.0% in the 12:15:00Z bucket and stays pinned at 100% for all 46 subsequent buckets; success_rate collapses 99.7%→~2.5% at the same bucket

All 311 ERROR entries share one identical signature — 'remote error: tls: expired certificate (alert 45); our client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z' — first at 12:15:27Z, the expiration instant matching the metric step exactly
Failed transfers are marked PENDING_RETRY instead of returning HTTP 5xx, so the 5xx-only error_rate stays 0.1–0.32 and the dashboard reads green
Business-level impact matches the ~40 tickets: 311 payment-service ERRORs (~8x the tickets, several per failed transfer) and ~2.5% success rate from 12:15Z onward

assumptions: RESIDUAL (unresolved, carried explicitly per critique): no finding establishes whether the cert was actually renewed/reloaded. The 'renewed-but-not-reloaded / stale TLS context' sub-branch cannot be excluded by direct secret inspection — no cert-manager, no TLS-secret object, no CRL/renewal-job record is reachable in this tooling. If that sub-branch is true the owning fix shifts to a config-reload/rollout, though the origin service stays payment-service.

RESIDUAL (unfalsifiable with available telemetry): a coincident bank-side change at exactly 12:15:00Z cannot be excluded — bank-partner-api has has_telemetry=false, so our evidence is one-sided (caller-side). Carried as an accepted risk, not treated as ruled out.

Sibling services holding the same/sibling client cert were not positively checked: only keyword log searches ('cert','bank') returned 0 for settlement-service and order-service, and portfolio-service's bank search exhausted budget. A shared CA/secret-issuer origin is bounded only by log silence, not cleared by metric evidence.

No payment-service pod restart/reload event feed or latency/cpu/memory/restart metrics were reachable within budget; resource pressure as a co-factor cannot be fully excluded (though request_rate and db_pool_in_use are flat).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Bank/acquirer-side outage (external dependency failure) masked from our dashboard
ranked_hypotheses.statement: bank-partner-api itself degraded at ~12:15:00Z (outage, 5xx, or refused handshakes), independent of our certificate state. Because bank-partner-api exposes no telemetry and payment-service surfaces bank failures as PENDING_RETRY rather than HTTP 5xx, an external outage would also present as 'customers report failures, our dashboard green'.

causal_chain.claim: bank-partner-api is the terminal external dependency with has_telemetry=false, so any bank-side failure is invisible except through its callers
Failures on the external bank edge after the HTTP response is formed do not increment payment-service's HTTP error_rate, producing the green-dashboard pattern
Precedent HIST-105 (2025-11-19): payment failures caused by bank partner API returning 5xx for 40 minutes; resolution was to wait for the partner
bank_api_error_rate steps to 100% at 12:15:00Z and payment_success_rate collapses to ~2.5%

assumptions: That TLS alert 45 'expired certificate' naming OUR client cert and its notAfter could be produced by bank-side behaviour — the alert-45/notAfter text and the historical-precedent mismatch (HIST-105 was 5xx, not TLS) both argue against this
That the exact 12:15:00Z step coinciding with our notAfter is coincidence
Bank-side telemetry is unobtainable, so this hypothesis cannot be positively excluded — it is only out-ranked

ranked_hypotheses.title: cfg-2502 (bank.api.timeout_ms 3000→5000 at 11:20:00Z) triggering the payment failures
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The only config change in the window — raising payment-service's bank.api.timeout_ms from 3000 to 5000 ms at 2026-04-02T11:20:00Z 'after partner advisory' — altered timeout/retry behaviour on the bank edge, causing transfers to fail or be retried into failure, with failures recorded outside the HTTP 5xx path so the error panel stays green.

causal_chain.claim: cfg-2502 raised bank.api.timeout_ms 3000→5000 at 11:20:00Z, ~10 minutes before the observation window start
Longer bank-call timeouts change retry/handling behaviour on the bank egress edge
Transfers begin failing and are marked PENDING_RETRY rather than returned as 5xx, keeping error_rate flat
bank_api_error_rate steps to 100% at 12:15:00Z and success rate collapses

assumptions: That a timeout increase could cause a hard, total 100% rejection — a timeout cannot produce an instant hard-fail at a precise later second
That no better mechanism explains the 12:15:00Z step

CHECKABLE GAP (per critique): the content of the 'partner advisory' behind cfg-2502 is unresolved; if it mentioned credential rotation or endpoint/TLS changes, this change becomes a contributing factor rather than an innocent bystander
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Timing and mechanism both fail. The change precedes symptom onset by ~55–72 minutes with a healthy 11:45–12:12 baseline (~0.2% bank_api_error_rate); a 3000→5000 ms timeout increase cannot cause a hard 100% failure beginning precisely at the certificate's notAfter instant; and the error text is a TLS expired-certificate rejection (alert 45), not a timeout. Note the residual research item: the advisory's content is unread.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared downstream component (ledger-db / kafka) failing post-response, silently failing transfers
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A shared component used by payment-service and neighbours — ledger-db (postgres) or kafka — degraded so transfers were committed on the HTTP path but failed afterwards, producing customer-visible failures with a normal HTTP error_rate. A neighbouring service on the same shared component would be the origin of the degradation.

causal_chain.claim: ledger-db and kafka are shared downstream of payment-service and also used by order-service, portfolio-service, settlement-service and notification-service
Failures occurring after the synchronous HTTP response is returned do not increment payment-service's own error_rate, matching the green-dashboard pattern
Precedent HIST-114 (ledger-db disk-full from retained WAL) shows this class of failure is possible
Transfers fail while the dashboard stays green

assumptions: That a DB or broker failure could manifest as TLS handshake rejections against bank-partner-api — not plausible
That the exact 12:15:00Z onset coincides with the cert notAfter
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Contradicted by scope and mechanism. Neighbours on the shared components show no matching symptom — settlement-service only 3 non-payment WARNs (GC/clock) from 12:44Z, order-service 2 WARNs, notification-service zero, and keyword searches for 'cert'/'bank' in settlement- and order-service return 0 (F17, F19, F20, F21, F22). request_rate and db_pool_in_use are flat with no step at onset (F11). All 311 errors are TLS alert 45 expired-certificate rejections on the bank edge, which a DB or broker failure cannot produce (F10, F13, F14).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Client-app issue: malformed requests / client-side misreporting (reporter's suspicion)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The ~40 support tickets reflect a client application problem — malformed or wrongly signed requests rejected client-side, or the app misreporting success/failure — so the server-side error rate stays normal.

causal_chain.claim: Client app produces malformed requests or misreports transfer outcomes
Server-side HTTP error_rate therefore stays normal
Customers report failures

assumptions: That server logs would not record the failures — false; 311 ERRORs on the bank edge are recorded
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: The failures are demonstrably server-side and pervasive: payment_success_rate collapses to ~2.5% (F8, F16) and 311 payment-service ERRORs all carry the identical expired-client-certificate TLS rejection from bank-partner-api (F13, F14). The green panel is explained by the 5xx-only metric definition plus PENDING_RETRY handling, not by absent server-side failure.

facts.statement: All 311 payment-service ERRORs from 12:15:27Z to 13:58:39Z share one identical signature rooted in payment-service's own client certificate: 'remote error: tls: expired certificate (alert 45); our client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z'.

The expiration instant of the client certificate (2026-04-02T12:15:00Z) exactly matches the metric onset: bank_api_error_rate steps from ~0.20% (stable 11:45–12:12) to 100.0% at the 12:15:00Z bucket and stays pinned at 100% through 13:57:00Z.
payment_success_rate collapses at the same bucket, from ~99.45% at 12:00 to ~2.49% at 12:15 and ~2–3% thereafter — the true business-level symptom.
The HTTP error_rate metric (defined as % of HTTP 5xx) stays flat at 0.1–0.32 across all 135 points and reads 0.29 at 12:33:00Z, which is why the dashboard appeared green.

Failures occur outside the synchronous HTTP path: failed transfers are marked PENDING_RETRY internally rather than surfaced as 5xx, consistent with error_rate staying ~0.2% while bank_api_error_rate is 100% and success rate is ~2.5%.

The request path is otherwise healthy: request_rate is steady ~100 req/s (no dip at 12:15) and db_pool_in_use is flat ~8 connections, so neither request volume nor DB/connection pool explains the failures.

Exactly one deployment (settlement-service v1.9.0, 2026-04-02T10:30:00Z) and exactly one config change (cfg-2502, bank.api.timeout_ms 3000→5000 on payment-service at 11:20:00Z) occurred across all services in 04-01T00:00Z–04-02T13:59Z; neither touches payment-service's TLS credential.

No certificate-management service exists in the monitored estate: get_config_changes and get_service_dependencies for 'cert-manager' both returned not_found, and no secret-rotation or renewal-job entity is present in known_services.

payment-service's dependency map has no certificate/secret/CA node; its outbound edges are ledger-db (db), bank-partner-api (external, has_telemetry false, owner vendor) and kafka (queue-produce), so the mTLS credential is internal to payment-service and not observable as a separate dependency.

No sibling service shows a matching symptom: settlement-service logged only 3 WARNs (GC/clock, none before 12:15Z), order-service 2 WARNs, portfolio-service 1 WARN, notification-service 0; keyword searches for 'cert' and 'bank' in settlement-service and order-service returned 0 matches.
A cert-watcher WARN at 11:50:26Z gave 25-minute advance notice that the client certificate would expire at 12:15:00Z.
bank-partner-api is a terminal external dependency with has_telemetry=false, so bank-side state cannot be observed directly — only through its caller, payment-service.

The interpretation that the fault is payment-service-internal at the TLS client-credential layer (our expired cert, not a bank outage) is supported: the remote returned 'expired certificate (alert 45)' naming our cert, the 100% step coincides exactly with notAfter, and no bank-side 5xx/timeout signature appears (unlike precedent HIST-105, which was 5xx-based).

assumptions: RESIDUAL (unresolved, carried explicitly per critique): no finding establishes whether the certificate was actually renewed/reloaded. The 'renewed but not reloaded / stale TLS context' sub-branch cannot be excluded by direct secret inspection — no cert-manager, no TLS-secret object, and no CRL/renewal-job record is reachable with this tooling. If that sub-branch is true, the owning fix shifts to a config-reload/rollout, but the origin service remains payment-service.

RESIDUAL (unfalsifiable with available telemetry): a coincident bank-side change at exactly 12:15:00Z cannot be excluded, because bank-partner-api exposes no telemetry and our evidence is caller-side only. Carried as an accepted risk, not treated as ruled out.

Sibling services holding the same or a sibling client certificate were not positively checked: keyword log searches ('cert','bank') returned 0 for settlement-service and order-service, and portfolio-service's 'bank' search exhausted budget. A shared CA/secret-issuer origin is bounded only by log silence, not cleared by metric evidence.

No payment-service pod restart/reload event feed or latency/cpu/memory/restart metrics were reachable within budget, so resource pressure as a co-factor cannot be fully excluded (though request_rate and db_pool_in_use are flat).
The ~40 support tickets versus 311 logged ERRORs is an approximation: the ERROR count mixes 'PENDING_RETRY' marks and 'call failed' lines, so the unique failed-transfer count is not exact.

timeline.event: Only deployment in the wider window: settlement-service v1.9.0 ('new CSV exporter') by ci-bot; unrelated to payment-service TLS.
Only config change in the window: cfg-2502 raises payment-service bank.api.timeout_ms 3000→5000 ms ('after partner advisory'). No cert/TLS key changed.
Advance-notice WARN: cert-watcher reports client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal expires in 25 minutes (notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z).
Last healthy bucket: bank_api_error_rate ~0.20% and payment_success_rate ~99.45%.
Certificate notAfter instant: bank_api_error_rate steps to 100.0% and payment_success_rate collapses to ~2.5%; HTTP error_rate (5xx-only) remains flat ~0.2–0.3%.
Earliest incident ERROR: 'payment 45f233b6 marked PENDING_RETRY: mTLS handshake with bank-partner-api rejected'.
Incident reported by support lead: ~40 tickets for failed fund transfers while payment-service error-rate panel shows nothing unusual.
First of only 3 settlement-service WARNs (GC pause), unrelated to the 12:15 onset; neighbouring services remain symptom-free.
bank_api_error_rate still pinned at 100% and the last of 311 ERRORs logged, confirming persistent 100% rejection on the bank egress.

recommended_actions.action: Immediate mitigation: issue and deploy a valid replacement client certificate for CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal to payment-service (rotate/renew the TLS client credential) and confirm the running pods serve the new cert — options are a new Kubernetes TLS secret mounted into payment-service or a payment-service config reload/restart, since no cert-manager entity exists in the estate.
recommended_actions.rationale: The only change in the estate tied to the 12:15Z step and to all 311 identical errors is our own client cert expiring at 12:15:00Z; until a valid cert is served, 100% of bank-egress transfers are hard-rejected with TLS alert 45.

recommended_actions.action: Immediate mitigation: verify bank-api recovery after cert replacement by watching payment-service bank_api_error_rate return to ~0.2% and payment_success_rate return to ~99%+, and by confirming the 'tls: expired certificate (alert 45)' ERROR stream stops.
recommended_actions.rationale: bank_api_error_rate pinned at 100% and success rate ~2.5% are the verified business-level indicators of the failure; they are the fastest confirmation the mitigation worked.

recommended_actions.action: Immediate mitigation: drain/retry the backlog of transfers marked PENDING_RETRY, and reconcile with support's ~40 tickets to identify and re-drive customer-visible failed transfers.
recommended_actions.rationale: Failed transfers were queued internally as PENDING_RETRY rather than surfaced, so customer-visible failures must be re-driven after credential recovery.

recommended_actions.action: Short-term: fix the silent-failure observability gap — alert on bank_api_error_rate and payment_success_rate (not just HTTP-5xx error_rate), and add the cert-watcher expiry WARN as a paging alert with meaningful lead time.
recommended_actions.rationale: The dashboard stayed green throughout because error_rate counts only HTTP 5xx while the fault occurred on the bank egress and was recorded as PENDING_RETRY; the existing 11:50:26Z cert-watcher WARN gave notice but did not page anyone.

recommended_actions.action: Short-term: confirm which sub-origin applies (never-renewed vs renewed-but-not-reloaded) by inspecting the payment-service TLS secret's creation/update timestamp and current notAfter, and checking for pod restarts/reloads; if the cert was already renewed, the fix moves to a config-reload/rollout of payment-service.
recommended_actions.rationale: This is the one unresolved detail of H1's chain and it determines whether the durable fix is renewal automation or a reload/rollout mechanism.

recommended_actions.action: Short-term: read the 'partner advisory' referenced in cfg-2502 (bank.api.timeout_ms 3000→5000 at 11:20:00Z) to check whether it mentioned credential rotation or endpoint/TLS changes; treat it as innocent unless the content proves otherwise.
recommended_actions.rationale: cfg-2502 is the only config change in the window and its content is unread; timing and mechanism already exonerate it as the driver, but the advisory content is a checkable gap flagged by the Critic.

recommended_actions.action: Long-term: introduce automated client-certificate renewal (an actual cert-manager/rotation job or equivalent) with expiry alerting well ahead of notAfter, so the payment-service→bank-partner-api mTLS credential never depends on manual action.
recommended_actions.rationale: No renewal artifact exists anywhere in the change feed and no certificate-management service is present in the estate; the closest precedent HIST-106 was 'client certificate expired; no renewal automation' — the same class of failure.

recommended_actions.action: Long-term: inventory which services hold a bank-partner-api or sibling client certificate and their notAfter values, and add cert-expiry dashboards per service, to bound the blast radius of any shared-CA or shared-issuer expiry.
recommended_actions.rationale: Sibling services were only cleared by keyword log silence (0 'cert'/'bank' matches) and no positive evidence exists that they hold different certs or expiry dates, so the single-cert vs shared-CA discrimination remains open.

recommended_actions.action: Long-term: establish bank-side observability or a partner-side synthetic canary against bank-partner-api, since it exposes no telemetry and can only be observed through its caller.
recommended_actions.rationale: The inability to see the bank side is what keeps a coincident bank-side event at 12:15:00Z unfalsifiable and forces reliance on caller-side inference.

data_gaps: No telemetry exists for bank-partner-api (has_telemetry false, vendor-owned): its error rates, latency and 5xx status around 11:30–12:30 could not be queried, so a coincident bank-side fault cannot be confirmed or excluded.

The available_metrics list and time series for ledger-db, kafka, settlement-service and payment-service were never pulled (budget exhausted), so the exact onset time and first-deviating shared component could not be established independently of the payment-service metrics.
The maintenance/change window before 2026-04-01 was not queried and change-freeze/notification records were not inspected, so a change older than 01 Apr cannot be ruled out as a contributing trigger.
Historical incident search returned only 5 hits (top match_score 2); a broader query for the 'green dashboard'/silent post-response failure pattern was not run, so an exact prior match may exist.
api-gateway and other neighbour services were not queried for anomalies at 12:15:00Z, so blast radius beyond payment-service is unestablished.

latency_p99_ms, cpu_pct, memory_pct and restart counts for payment-service could not be pulled, so resource pressure/restarts as a co-factor cannot be fully excluded (though request_rate and db_pool_in_use are flat).
No bank_api_latency_ms metric exists for payment-service, so any pre-12:15 latency drift on the bank edge (which would distinguish partial degradation from a hard 100% reject) could not be measured.

Sibling services' bank_api_error_rate/TLS metrics and their client-certificate notAfter values were not retrieved, so a shared CA/secret issuer vs payment-service-own cert lifecycle remains bounded only by log silence.

The literal question of whether the TLS secret still holds the expired cert (notAfter=12:15:00Z) or a newer one could not be answered — no cert-manager service, TLS-secret object or renewal-job entity is reachable in this tooling.
No payment-service pod restart/reload event feed is available, so the 'renewed but not reloaded' sub-branch of H1 could not be checked directly.
The unique failed-transfer count is approximate: the 311 ERROR entries mix PENDING_RETRY marks and call-failed lines, so the ticket-vs-actual-failure ratio is an estimate.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: A valid, unexpired client certificate found in payment-service's TLS secret with notAfter after 12:15:00Z on 2026-04-02 would indicate the cert was renewed and the fault is a stale TLS context / missing reload, shifting the fix to a config-reload/rollout (origin service unchanged).

Evidence of a bank-partner-api-side outage or 5xx/refused-handshake episode at exactly 12:15:00Z — e.g. vendor incident notice or a matching caller-side 5xx signature — would support H2 (external dependency failure) over H1.

Discovery that settlement-service, order-service or portfolio-service also stepped to 100% bank_api_error_rate at exactly 12:15:00Z, or that they share the same client cert/notAfter, would indicate a shared CA/secret-issuer failure rather than payment-service's own credential lifecycle.

A payment-service pod restart or TLS-context reload event coinciding with renewal would establish the 'renewed-but-not-reloaded' sub-origin and change the immediate remediaction from cert issuance to a forced reload/rollout.

A verified bank_api_call latency increase or partial failure on the bank edge before 12:15:00Z (if bank_api_latency_ms existed) would indicate partial degradation rather than a hard, total reject at the cert notAfter instant.
Evidence that the failures were not TLS-related at all — e.g. server-side logs showing a different error class or confirming the failures were client-side — would overturn H1 in favour of H5.

findings.statement: No deployments occurred in the 11:30–12:30 window: get_deployments for 2026-04-02T11:00Z–12:40Z across all services returned count 0. Widening to 2026-04-01T00:00Z–2026-04-02T13:59Z returned exactly one deployment, settlement-service v1.9.0 ('new CSV exporter') deployed at 2026-04-02T10:30:00Z by ci-bot, status 'live' with rolled_back_at null.

Exactly one config/flag change in the whole 04-01→04-02T13:59 window: cfg-2502 on payment-service, key bank.api.timeout_ms, raised 3000 → 5000 ms at 2026-04-02T11:20:00Z by author p.nair, 'Raise bank API timeout after partner advisory'. That is 10 minutes before the 11:30 window start and ~72 minutes before the 12:32 report. No other service had a config change.

payment-service dependency map: edges are payment-service → ledger-db (db), payment-service → bank-partner-api (external, has_telemetry false, owner vendor), payment-service → kafka (queue-produce), and api-gateway → payment-service (http). bank-partner-api is the terminal external dependency and exposes no telemetry, so bank-side failures cannot be confirmed from our data.

Two SHARED components sit downstream of payment-service and are used by other services: ledger-db (postgres, shared true) also written/read by order-service, portfolio-service and settlement-service; kafka (shared true) is produced to by order-service and payment-service, and consumed by settlement-service and notification-service. A neighbour on either shared component can affect transfers at a point after the synchronous HTTP response is returned.

Relevant precedent found: HIST-105 (2025-11-19) 'Payment failures: bank partner API outage', services [payment-service], symptoms ['payment failures','bank api errors'], root cause 'Bank partner API returned 5xx for 40 minutes (their incident)', category dependency_failure, resolution 'Waited for partner; queued retries'. The search also returned HIST-114 ledger-db disk-full from retained WAL (resource_exhaustion), HIST-106 settlement mTLS cert expiry, and HIST-109 auth JWT regression. Note the search explicitly warns: past incidents are leads, not evidence about the current incident.

The expiration instant (12:15:00Z) exactly matches the metric onset step.

Onset correlation is exact: bank_api_error_rate holds steady ~0.2% through the 12:12:00Z bucket, then steps to 100.0% at 12:15:00Z and stays pinned at 100% for all 46 subsequent buckets through 13:57:00Z (min 0.19, max 100, mean 77.82). The single config change (bank.api.timeout_ms 3000->5000 at 11:20:00Z, ~55 min earlier) cannot produce a 100% hard-fail that begins precisely at the cert notAfter instant; the expiry timestamp does.

Business-level success is destroyed immediately: payment_success_rate reads 99.45% at the 12:00 bucket then ~2.5% for every bucket from 12:16 onward (12:16 avg 2.55, last 2.13; min 1.44), confirming the vast majority of transfers after onset fail.

The fault is confined to the payment-service -> bank-partner-api egress edge; neighbouring services on shared components show no matching symptom. settlement-service logged only 3 WARNs (GC pause / clock drift) from 12:44:09Z, and order-service only 1 WARN (GC pause) at 12:48:21Z -- none coincident with or before 12:15:00Z and none payment-related. This argues against a shared ledger-db/kafka failure as the driver.

Interpretation: the evidence supports a PAYMENT-SERVICE-INTERNAL fault at the TLS client-credential layer (our own expired client cert), NOT a bank/gateway-side outage. The remote returned 'expired certificate (alert 45)', i.e. the bank correctly rejected our expired cert rather than the bank being down; the 100% step at exactly notAfter=12:15:00Z and the identical driver signature across all 311 errors localize the cause to payment-service's cert/secret management. No bank-side error (5xx/timeout) signature appears anywhere, unlike precedent HIST-105.

refs.quote: remote error: tls: expired certificate (alert 45); our client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z

findings.statement: settlement-service logs between 2026-04-02T11:45Z and 13:59Z contain only 3 WARN entries, none before 12:15:00Z and none payment/TLS related: 'GC pause 391ms exceeded 200ms target' at 12:44:09Z, 'clock drift 38ms detected, resyncing with NTP' at 13:08:13Z, and 'GC pause 246ms exceeded 200ms target' at 13:41:37Z.

order-service logs in the same window contain only 2 WARNs — 'slow request 5211ms on /internal/metrics' at 11:52:42Z and 'GC pause 406ms exceeded 200ms target' at 12:48:21Z — neither at 12:15:00Z nor TLS/bank related; portfolio-service shows 1 WARN ('GC pause 427ms exceeded 200ms target', 11:52:31Z).
notification-service logged 0 entries at WARN or above for 2026-04-02T08:00–13:59Z, so it shows no symptom related to the 12:15Z onset.

Keyword searches for 'cert' in settlement-service and order-service over 2026-04-02T08:00–13:59Z return 0 matches, and searches for 'bank' in settlement-service and order-service also return 0 matches — i.e. no TLS-45/expired-certificate signature and no bank_api call evidence in the neighbouring services.

No neighbour of payment-service exhibits a TLS alert-45 / expired-certificate error or any bank-related error step at 12:15:00Z; the only 12:15Z step observed anywhere is on payment-service's own bank_api_error_rate (established in F7/F15, step to 100%). This is consistent with payment-service's own client-cert expiry rather than a service-wide CA/secret failure, but the neighbours' absence of logs alone does not rule out a shared issuer.

No certificate-management service exists in the monitored estate: get_config_changes and get_service_dependencies for 'cert-manager' both returned not_found, with the known_services list containing no cert-manager, secret-rotation or renewal-job entity (only 18 application/infra services such as payment-service, ledger-db, kafka, bank-partner-api).

No renewal-related deployment occurred for payment-service: get_deployments for payment-service over 2026-04-01T00:00Z–2026-04-02T13:59Z returned count 0, so no cert-rotation/rollout release was deployed to the service in that window.

The only config change in the entire window is unrelated to certificates: cfg-2502 on payment-service, key bank.api.timeout_ms 3000 -> 5000 at 2026-04-02T11:20:00Z. No config key referencing TLS secret, certificate mount, or notAfter appears, so no secret-mount or cert-path change was recorded.

Across ALL services the same two facts hold: exactly one deployment (dep-5510, settlement-service v1.9.0, 2026-04-02T10:30:00Z) and exactly one config change (cfg-2502) in 04-01T00:00Z–04-02T13:59Z. Neither touches payment-service's TLS credential, so no in-band renewal artifact (CertificateRequest creation, secret update, mount change) is visible anywhere in the change feed.

payment-service's dependency map contains no certificate/secret/CA node and no cert-manager edge — its outbound edges are ledger-db (db), bank-partner-api (external, has_telemetry false, owner vendor) and kafka (queue-produce). The mTLS credential used against bank-partner-api is therefore internal to payment-service and not observable as a separate dependency in this tooling.

The closest precedent to H1 is HIST-106 (2025-06-30, settlement-service) 'Settlement mTLS certificate expired', symptoms ['tls handshake failures','expired certificate'], root_cause 'Client certificate expired; no renewal automation', resolution 'Issued new cert; added expiry alert'. The precedent is a lead only, and notably HIST-108 shows a rotation-rollout class ('Key rotation published new key id before all pods loaded the JWKS') distinct from a never-renewed class.
